title: She loved the man God chose…
paragraphs:
She loved the man God chose…
and still ended up bitter, empty, and spiritually cold.

Because most people think loving a godly person automatically guarantees joy. They think proximity to calling equals intimacy with God. They think being connected to an anointed person means their own heart is safe.
She loved David. Scripture says it plainly. Not one of Saul’s servants. Not one of the women in Israel. Michal loved David.
But by the end of her story, she became a woman consumed with contempt, sarcasm, and barrenness.
Because somewhere along the way, her love for David stopped being rooted in love for God.
The first time we see Michal, there’s passion.
David was the rising warrior. The giant slayer. The worshiper. The man women sang about in the streets.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You can admire God’s anointed and still carry the spirit of Saul inside you.
Michal grew up in Saul’s house. A house filled with jealousy, image protection, insecurity, and rebellion against God. Even though she loved David, she had still been shaped by Saul’s atmosphere.
And eventually, what’s inside you always surfaces.
That’s why some people start passionate in faith… then slowly become critical, cold, offended, and empty.
Still know how to look spiritual.
But joy disappears because their heart stopped bowing before God long ago.
The breaking point came during one of the most powerful moments in David’s life.
The Ark of the Covenant was finally returning to Jerusalem.

“And David danced before the Lord with all his might.”
— 2 Samuel 6:14
David understood something Michal never did:
The presence of God is worth looking foolish for.
But Michal watched from a window.
And some people have spent so long watching worship that they forgot how to worship themselves.
They stand at a distance criticizing surrendered people because deep down they’re uncomfortable with intimacy toward God.
When David returned home, overflowing with joy after honoring God, Michal met him with contempt.

“‘How the king of Israel honored himself today, uncovering himself today before the eyes of his servants’ female servants, as one of the vulgar fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!’”
— 2 Samuel 6:20
One person left God’s presence alive.
The other stayed spiritually dead behind a window.
Some people secretly resent radical worship because it exposes their own deadness.
Mock people who genuinely burn for Jesus.
Not because those believers are wrong.
Michal couldn’t understand why David would lower himself before God.
But David answered with words that expose the entire tragedy of her heart:
David feared God more than people.
Michal feared dignity more than distance from God.
You can feel the spiritual decay in her response.
That is what happens when pride hardens the soul.
And pride rarely announces itself loudly at first.
But underneath it is resistance toward surrender.
And eventually, people who truly love Jesus start making you uncomfortable.
That’s a dangerous place to be.
Because the issue was never David’s dancing.
And Scripture ends her story with one devastating sentence:

“And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.”
— 2 Samuel 6:23
A heart that once loved David but eventually despised the very worship that kept David alive.
This is why proximity to anointed people cannot save you.
Your spouse’s faith cannot save you.
Your pastor’s fire cannot save you.
Your Christian family cannot save you.
You must personally love the presence of God.
Because church culture without heart transformation eventually produces bitterness.
You can be close to worship and still never enter it.
Close to truth and still reject it.
Close to David and still miss God.
But the Gospel tells a different story.
Jesus Christ came for proud, critical, spiritually barren people like us.
Because if we’re honest, many of us have had moments where we stood at the window too.
But Jesus steps into dead hearts and offers mercy.
The cross destroys pride because it forces you to admit you cannot save yourself.
Your religious performance cannot save you.
And the resurrection proves that dead things can live again.
You cannot cling to pride and intimacy with God at the same time.
And many people already know which one they’ve been protecting.
Maybe that’s why worship feels uncomfortable now.
Maybe that’s why conviction irritates you instead of softening you.
Maybe that’s why passionate believers secretly bother you.
Because something inside you remembers what closeness to God once felt like.
To joy that criticism can never produce.
The enemy wants you at the window.
Jesus calls you into His presence.
If this exposed something in you, don’t ignore it. Somebody else reading may realize they’re not alone in their spiritual dryness.
